title: AI Agents & Agentic Systems
summary: Autonomous systems that combine reasoning traces with action/tool interaction patterns to solve multi-step problems through planning, execution, and observation loops.
historicalContext: Early LLM integrations were passive, answering queries in a single turn without the ability to plan, use tools, or correct errors. This limitation motivated Yao et al. in 2022 to introduce the ReAct (Reason + Act) paradigm—allowing models to generate reasoning traces, choose tools, and observe environment outputs iteratively to solve complex tasks.

landmarkReferences.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
landmarkReferences.contribution: Combined reasoning traces with action/tool interaction patterns.

commonMisconceptions.wrong: Agents are inherently reliable decision makers for multi-step goals.
commonMisconceptions.correct: Agents lack genuine intuition; they act based on prompt instructions and statistical next-token predictions, making them prone to looping without continuous feedback safeguards.

analogies.text: An agent loop is like an engineer sitting at a terminal, running a command, reading the error, and correcting their code before running it again.
analogies.limitations: Engineers understand the target goal, whereas agent systems execute token predictions without conscious intent.

curiosityFacts: Did you know that the ReAct loop was inspired by human cognitive behaviors? We write down intermediate steps (thoughts) and run commands (actions) when solving math problems.
In 1950, Alan Turing described the 'Turing Test,' but he also envisioned an agentic structure where programs could modify their own instructions based on feedback.
storySeeds: The domain transitioned from passive text prediction models to active decision-making loops that interact with external operating systems and APIs.
Agent systems transformed passive text prediction APIs into active software systems that plan, interact with databases, and correct their own errors.
assessmentSeeds: Contrast the planning behavior of a ReAct agent loop with linear directed acyclic graph (DAG) routing.
What security risks arise when giving LLM agents direct tool access without sandboxing?
professionalInsights: Isolate tool execution in self-contained worker pools and use asynchronous queues to manage long-running planning steps.
Audit agent traces to monitor step execution count, token usage, tool errors, and flag infinite execution loops in production.
An operations automation agent was modified from a free-form ReAct model to a structured routing graph. This reduced task failure rates from 30% to less than 2% by restricting tool paths.
